tasks.short: Recommend resolution of product or process deviations.

steps.what: Show deviations from established process standards
Recommend resolution of identified product deviations

outputs: filed copy of signed deviation resolution v1

tasks.design: A job shows stored deviations against the process standards in {DATA_PLATFORM}. The engineer recommends the resolution. A model does not close the deviation. The engineer signs the note in {DOCS}, and a later job files that version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Deviation lists were rebuilt before anyone could recommend a resolution.
tasks.enabler_now: Deviation rows and the standard limits are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The right resolution can sit outside the standard text.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer decides the recommendation and whether production may continue.

ambition.what: Recommend a resolution the day a stored deviation repeats.

tasks.altitude: The engineer spends the week on the recommendation, not on rebuilding the list.

evidence.claim: The engineering digest says test data and root-cause work can use a dashboard and statistics on recorded measurements, and the engineer still decides the cause.
The engineering digest says advice, design, and research stay manual, and the signing engineer stays responsible.

assumptions: Standards are stored as limits, not only as prose.
Configure the existing record before a new store.
unknowns: Who else must accept a resolution.
Whether a deviation stops the line.
research_questions: How often a deviation has no stored standard.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining recommendation time is still the engineer's judgement.

incremental.description: Remap source fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes standards are rarely stored as limits. The high end assumes standards are usually stored as limits. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design validation study sampling and test methods.

steps.what: List earlier sampling and testing features
Specify sampling, testing, and analytical methodologies
Sign the study design for this version

outputs: filed copy of signed study design v1

tasks.design: A job lists earlier study features from {DOCS}. The engineer designs the validation study, including sampling, testing, and analytical methodologies. A later job files only the signed design.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier studies were hard to find, and the method still has to be designed.
tasks.enabler_now: Prior study records can be listed without a new store.
tasks.still_hard: A new product may need a method no earlier study used.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer chooses the sample, the test, and the method.

ambition.what: Start from earlier features instead of a blank method sheet.

tasks.altitude: The engineer spends the week on the method, not on finding old studies.

reach.learn: Which sample size the design froze

evidence.claim: The engineering digest says advice, design, and research stay manual, and the signing engineer stays responsible.

assumptions: Earlier studies are stored and searchable.
Configure that store before a new one.
unknowns: Which analytical method the laboratory can run.
Whether a statistician must review the sample.
research_questions: How often a new product has no earlier study.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining design time is still the engineer's method choice.

incremental.description: Remap source fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes few earlier studies are stored. The high end assumes most products have an earlier study. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare qualification protocols for manufacturing processes.

steps.what: Cover modified manufacturing processes and equipment
Draft protocol text from stored requirement rows

loop.purpose: Draft protocol text from the engineer's outline and stored requirement rows.
loop.input: The outline and stored requirement rows.
loop.output: Protocol text in which every figure cites a requirement row.
loop.check: Every figure matches a stored requirement row.
loop.stop: Stop when a figure has no requirement row.
loop.why_not_simpler: A blank protocol form cannot carry the method the engineer chose.

steps.what: Include pharmaceuticals, electronics, and other products
Sign the validation protocol for production

outputs: filed copy of signed validation protocol v1

tasks.design: The engineer prepares the performance qualification protocol for the modified process and the equipment in {DOCS}. A bounded draft uses stored requirement rows and stops when a figure has no row. For a pharmaceutical computerised system, the engineer signs before a later job files that version. The vendor cycle-time figure is not this saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Protocols were copied from the last product, including figures that did not belong to this process.
tasks.enabler_now: Requirement rows can be cited by identifier.
tasks.still_hard: A pharmaceutical computerised system needs the engineer's own check, not a generated protocol.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer decides the protocol and signs it.

ambition.what: Prepare the next protocol from stored requirements without copying the last product's figures.

tasks.altitude: The engineer spends the week on the protocol scope, not on retyping stored requirements.

reach.learn: Which product family the protocol covers

evidence.claim: The engineering digest says an artefact generator fills templates from records, a model may draft prose, every number must trace to a record, and the engineer signs.
Digest [S15] says GMP Annex 11 governs computerised systems in pharmaceutical manufacture, so a protocol for such a system is signed before it is filed.
Digest [S20] says the institution asked for a paper to be withdrawn because it had no confidence in the data, so a generated number is not a record.
Digest [S7] is a vendor report of shorter validation cycles, and this design does not use that figure as its own labour saving.

assumptions: Pharmaceutical computerised systems follow the signed-protocol rule.
Configure the existing document store before a new one.
unknowns: Whether this protocol covers a computerised pharmaceutical system.
Who else must sign a protocol.
research_questions: How often electronics and pharmaceuticals share one protocol by mistake.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining protocol time is still the engineer's scope decision.

incremental.description: Remap source fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes requirement rows are sparse. The high end assumes requirement rows cover most protocol figures. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Create and populate validation tracking databases.

steps.what: Create database fields for validated systems
Maintain validation activities and test results
Sign the rows before the database write
Populate the tracking database with signed rows
outputs: filed copy of signed validation rows v1

tasks.design: The engineer creates the fields and chooses the validation activities and test results. A later job populates {DATA_PLATFORM} with only the signed rows. It does not edit a live row the engineer did not sign, and it is not an agent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tracking sheets were retyped into a database, and a live row could change with no signed set.
tasks.enabler_now: The database can take a signed batch of rows.
tasks.still_hard: A rejected result must stay out until the engineer signs a new set.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer decides which results are tracked and signs that set.

ambition.what: Load a signed result set the day the tests are accepted.

tasks.altitude: The engineer spends the week on what to track, not on retyping accepted rows.

reach.task: Keep the filed rows as the tracking copy
reach.learn: Which fields the signed set contains

evidence.claim: Digest [S5] is cited for coded rule checks on records and plan reviews, so blank protocol fields are listed before the engineer decides.
The engineering digest says advice, design, and research stay manual, and the signing engineer stays responsible.

assumptions: The job writes only the signed batch.
Configure the existing database before a new one.
unknowns: Who may reject a result after it is signed.
Whether validated-system status needs a second signature.
research_questions: How often a test result changes after the batch is signed.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining selection time is still the engineer choosing rows.

incremental.description: Remap source fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes results are not yet in a stable layout. The high end assumes results already match the field list. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The validation engineer spends the week on the test, the deviation, and the signed decision. Filing a signed record can move. A model does not release a protocol or change a live test station.
reach: Quality staff collect a sample only from the list the engineer signed.
A department starts a test only after the signed schedule is filed.
skills_to_grow: Reject a protocol figure that has no source row.
Leave equipment, sampling, and agency contact as their own work.
role.ambitious_version: A signed protocol or report can be filed the same day, and the engineer still releases it.
